title: Shortest word distance — repeated queries, then the same word twice
label: multi
statement: Build a structure from a list of words that answers, many times, **the shortest distance (difference in index) between two given words** in the list.
provenance: "Repeated shortest word distance queries" in a LinkedIn phone screen (Sep 2026, FastPrep) — LeetCode 244, which is on your LinkedIn-tagged list. Stage 2 is LeetCode 245 (the two words may be the same).

sources.name: FastPrep — LinkedIn interview questions, dated reports 2024–2026

clarify: Many queries on the same list? (Yes — that is the point.)
Are both words guaranteed to be present? (Throw if not.)
Can the two words be the same? (Stage 2.)

stages.title: Repeated queries
stages.say: Answer many shortest-distance queries on the same list of words.
stages.require: Implement `WordDistance(words)` and `Shortest(w1, w2)`. A missing word → `KeyNotFoundException`.

stages.title: The same word twice
stages.say: Now the two words may be the same — the distance between two different occurrences.
stages.require: `Shortest(w, w)` returns the smallest gap between two occurrences of w; a word that occurs once → `ArgumentException`.

prompts.label: Check my design — no code
prompts.text: I believe index every word's positions once in the constructor; each query then merges two sorted position lists with two pointers in O(a + b) instead of rescanning the whole list. Review my reasoning without giving me the implementation. What would break it?

prompts.label: Review, do not rewrite
prompts.text: Review my implementation for correctness and edge cases. Do not rewrite the code. List problems most severe first, each with the input that triggers it.

prompts.label: Race conditions
prompts.text: Now review this implementation for race conditions if multiple threads call Shortest concurrently. For each race, give the interleaving that breaks it. Then name the smallest synchronization boundary that preserves correctness. Do not write code yet.

prompts.label: Tests that expose bugs
prompts.text: Suggest tests that could expose bugs in my implementation: boundaries, duplicates, empty and invalid input, and concurrency where it applies. For each, say why the expected value is correct.

prompts.label: Complexity check
prompts.text: What is the time and space complexity of each public method as written? Do not claim a bound unless every step achieves it.

prompts.label: Requirement change
prompts.text: The requirement changed: Shortest(w, w) returns the smallest gap between two occurrences of w; a word that occurs once → ArgumentException. List which members need to change and which do not, before writing any code.

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: Build a structure from a list of words that answers, many times, **the shortest distance (difference in index) between two given words** in the list.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Many queries on the same list? (Yes — that is the point.)
- Are both words guaranteed to be present? (Throw if not.)
- Can the two words be the same? (Stage 2.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: The list does not change between queries, so pay once: map each word to its sorted positions. Two sorted lists meet like a merge — always advance the smaller index, because the other side can only get closer.

learn.title: 4 · Approach

learn.title: 11 · AI usage strategy

- Delegate the mechanical parts only after the structure is fixed.

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- Rescanning the whole list per query (O(n) each).
- Comparing every pair of positions (O(a·b)).
- For the same-word case, returning 0.
